answer: Unique-execution receipts.** Each agent identity is derived from the hash of a solved, non-outsourceable computation whose input is a freshly sampled marble-pattern challenge, making every identity encode distinct costly work. A valid identity publishes a signal binding its output to that input, verified by peers against a rotating atlas of recent solutions to block replay. Attacker cost: one full solve per identity, plus storage and verification of each receipt, so mass cloning scales linearly in compute rather than in cheap registrations.
